comment: 28yo female, Fitzpatrick skin type II, extensive recreational UV exposure history: weekly tanning-bed use ages 18-25 (~250 lifetime sessions, tanning-bed use before age 35 increases melanoma risk ~75% per IARC Group 1, 2009), multiple blistering sunburns in adolescence (≥6 lifetime), competitive beach-volleyball player with chronic recreational outdoor sun exposure summers. No current cancer diagnosis. UV — principal modifiable etiologic driver of cutaneous melanoma + BCC + SCC. Risk compounds with Fitzpatrick I-II, age >50 (still young here but cumulative-dose-based latency relevant), ≥5 lifetime sunburns doubles melanoma risk. Engine fires RF-LIFESTYLE-UV-EXPOSURE-PREVENTION (any_of: high_cumulative_uv_exposure:true OR tanning_bed_use_history:true OR history_blistering_sunburn:true OR fair_skin_fitzpatrick_i_ii:true OR occupational_outdoor_uv_exposure:true) and routes to PreventionPlan: standard = sun-protection counseling (broad-spectrum SPF ≥30 daily, photo-protective clothing, peak-UV-hour avoidance, tanning-bed cessation) + monthly patient skin self-exam education + clinical skin exam annually with dermatology baseline mole-mapping; alternative = counseling + symptom-triggered evaluation. Validates v0.3 lifestyle UV pilot (recreational/tanning-bed axis). Anchored DIS-MELANOMA + DIS-BCC.
